title: Sales playbook
author: Arjun Desai
text:
# Sales playbook
Owner: Arjun Desai (Sales). Last reviewed: 16 September 2026.
Who to ask: Arjun Desai for deal strategy, Daniel Lim for technical discovery, Nur Aziz for pricing exceptions, Nandini Wijaya for contract terms.

## Who we sell to
Northwind Labs sells shipment tracking and Route Lens arrival predictions to regional logistics operators that run their own depots. The buyer is usually a head of operations. The user is a dispatcher. The blocker is usually IT security or procurement.

## Stages
1. Qualify: confirm depot count, carrier mix and whether they already poll Kestrel. Owner: account executive.
2. Discovery: Daniel Lim runs the technical call. He records carrier list, event volume and data residency needs.
3. Pilot: a signed pilot order with fabricated shipments in a shared sandbox first, then live depots. Pilot success is measured in completed pilot shipments, which is the company Q4 outcome.
4. Proposal: price card plus any discount. Discounts follow the Discount approval matrix. Do not send a proposal with a discount above 10 percent before Finance approves it in writing.
5. Commit: record the customer procurement owner in CRM before moving a deal to commit. The CRM stage gate blocks the move if the field is empty.
6. Closed won: hand off to Siti Nuraini (Customer success) with the kickoff template.

## Price card (new subscriptions)
- Route Lens: USD 149 per workspace per month.
- Signed USD 99 pilots are honoured for six months from signature, then move to USD 149.
- SAML SSO is included in Enterprise. It is not a paid add-on, so never put it on a quote line.
- Platform tracking is billed once per completed shipment, not per tracking event.

## Things that lose deals
- Promising a guaranteed delivery time. Route Lens shows an estimated range, never a guarantee.
- Promising a launch date that Product has not published. Ask Aisha Rahman.
- Promising data residency we do not offer. Today only Sakura has a Japan-only contract schedule. Ask Nandini Wijaya before you discuss residency.

title: Discount approval matrix
author: Arjun Desai
text:
# Discount approval matrix
Owner: Arjun Desai. Finance approver: Nur Aziz. Effective 15 September 2026.
This page replaces the discount section of the Route Lens sales pricing deck.

## Matrix (Route Lens list price USD 149 per workspace per month)
- 0 to 10 percent: the account executive on the deal approves. Note the reason in the CRM discount field.
- Above 10 percent and up to 25 percent: written Finance approval from Nur Aziz before the proposal goes to the customer. Approval is a reply in the deal desk thread, not a verbal yes.
- Above 25 percent: written Finance approval from Nur Aziz and sign-off from Hana Okafor.
- Multi-year prepay terms: Nur Aziz, regardless of the discount level.
- Any contract worth more than USD 25000 annually also needs Legal review before signature (see Legal review thresholds and signatories).

## Why
In September we cut the AE discretionary band from 20 percent to 10 percent. The second inference pass on Route Lens leaves too little margin for the old band. Arjun Desai announced it in #sales on 8 September 2026.

## Not discounts
- Honouring a signed USD 99 pilot for six months is not a discount. Do not log it as one.
- SSO is included in Enterprise. Removing an SSO charge is not a discount, because there is no SSO charge.

Who to ask: Arjun Desai for the matrix, Nur Aziz for an approval.

title: Deal desk process
author: Nur Aziz
text:
# Deal desk process
Owners: Nur Aziz (Finance) and Arjun Desai (Sales). Legal reviewer: Nandini Wijaya. Last reviewed: 18 September 2026.

The deal desk is the #sales thread named "deal desk" plus a weekly 30 minute call on Wednesday at 10:00 SGT.

## When a deal goes to deal desk
- A discount above 10 percent.
- Payment terms other than net 30.
- Annual contract value above USD 25000 (Legal review).
- Any non-standard clause: residency, liability cap, custom subprocessor terms.

## Steps
1. The account executive posts the deal in the deal desk thread: customer, workspaces, term, discount, payment terms, and the CRM link.
2. Nur Aziz checks margin and payment terms. Approval is a written reply in the thread.
3. If Legal review is needed, Nandini Wijaya gets the redline in the Legal intake form. Target turnaround is three business days.
4. The account executive sends the proposal only after every needed approval is in the thread.
5. Nur Aziz attaches the approvals to the CRM opportunity before the stage moves to commit.

## Service levels
- Finance reply: one business day.
- Legal review: three business days for standard paper, five for customer paper.

title: CRM field guide
author: Arjun Desai
text:
# CRM field guide
Owner: Arjun Desai. Admin: Devika Fernando (Business operations). Last reviewed: 22 September 2026.

## Required fields by stage
- Qualify: company, depot count, carrier mix, source campaign.
- Discovery: technical contact, event volume estimate, residency requirement (yes or no and region).
- Pilot: pilot order number, pilot start date, pilot depots.
- Proposal: list price, discount percent, discount reason, Finance approval link when the discount is above 10 percent.
- Commit: customer procurement owner (name and email). The stage gate blocks commit when this field is empty.
- Closed won: signed order form, billing contact, payment terms.

## Field meanings
- Workspaces: the number of Route Lens workspaces on the order. Price is per workspace per month.
- Pilot rate flag: set when the customer has a signed USD 99 pilot. The flag expires six months after signature and Finance re-prices to USD 149.
- Active workspace: copied nightly from the warehouse. A workspace counts as active only when it completed at least one shipment in the calendar week. Ask Linh Nguyen about the definition.

## Hygiene
Devika Fernando runs a Monday report of deals in commit with no procurement owner. Fix them the same day.

title: Route Lens discovery call talk track

text:
# Route Lens discovery call talk track
Owner: Arjun Desai. Last reviewed: 10 June 2026.

## Opening (2 minutes)
Ask how dispatchers find out about late trucks today. Most say a phone call from the driver.

## Discovery questions
- How many depots, and which carriers feed them?
- Do you poll Kestrel today, or receive webhooks?
- Who signs software contracts, and who owns procurement?
- Do you have data residency requirements?

## Commercials
- List price is USD 149 per workspace per month. Signed USD 99 pilots keep their rate for six months.
- Account executives can approve Route Lens discounts up to 20 percent on the call to close the pilot quickly. Above that, bring in Nur Aziz.
- SSO is included in Enterprise.

## Close
Book the technical session with Daniel Lim before you hang up.

title: Support SLA tiers
author: Siti Nuraini
text:
# Support SLA tiers
Owner: Siti Nuraini (Customer success). Effective 16 September 2026.
Who to ask: Siti Nuraini for SLA terms, Daniel Lim for integration tickets, Mei Tan for incident command.

## Priorities
- P1: tracking or Route Lens down for a tenant, or data at risk.
- P2: a major feature degraded, workaround exists.
- P3: a minor defect or question.
- P4: a feature request.

## First response targets
- Enterprise P1: 15 minutes, 24x7, including weekends.
- Enterprise P2: 2 business hours. P3: 1 business day. P4: 5 business days.
- Standard P1: 1 hour during business hours (08:00 to 20:00 SGT, Monday to Saturday).
- Standard P2: 4 business hours. P3: 2 business days. P4: best effort.

## P1 handling
1. Page the incident commander immediately. Do not route P1 tickets to the customer success inbox first.
2. Then notify customer success in #support.
3. For a confirmed severity-one incident, the first customer notice goes out within 30 minutes of confirmation.

## Integration escalations
Every integration escalation carries the tenant ID and the last successful carrier event ID. Tickets without both go back to the submitter.

title: Hiring process
author: Amina Yusuf
text:
# Hiring process
Owner: Amina Yusuf (People operations). Effective 15 September 2026.
Who to ask: Amina Yusuf for process, the hiring manager for the role.

## Open roles
Permanent hiring is frozen except two support engineers and one data analyst (Hana Okafor, September 2026). Any other permanent role needs Hana Okafor to lift the freeze first.

## Interview loop: three rounds
1. Skills: a practical exercise with one interviewer from the team.
2. Collaboration: a pairing or case session with someone from a partner team.
3. Hiring-manager review: the hiring manager covers motivation, scope and level.

## Scorecards and debrief
- Every interviewer submits an independent scorecard before the hiring debrief starts. No scorecard, no seat in the debrief.
- Amina Yusuf runs the debrief. The hiring manager decides; Amina Yusuf can block for process reasons.

## Offer
- Level is set from the Career ladder and levels page.
- Offers are approved by the head of team and Amina Yusuf. Offers above band need Hana Okafor.

## Timeline
Target ten business days from first interview to offer.

title: Career ladder and levels
author: Amina Yusuf
text:
# Career ladder and levels
Owner: Amina Yusuf. Last reviewed: 1 July 2026.

Our org tree uses four levels: IC, lead, head, exec. Inside IC we use three steps.

## Levels
- IC 1: delivers well-scoped work with review. Example scope: a single feature or ticket queue.
- IC 2: owns a component end to end. Example: Kavya Iyer owns the regression suite.
- IC 3 (staff): sets technical direction across teams. Example: a staff platform engineer.
- Lead: owns a function or practice and coaches others. Examples: Linh Nguyen (Data), Jiwon Park (Security), Yuki Mori (Design), Farah Khan (Marketing), Devika Fernando (Operations).
- Head: owns a team, its budget and its hiring. Examples: Mei Tan (Engineering), Aisha Rahman (Product), Siti Nuraini (Customer success), Arjun Desai (Sales), Nur Aziz (Finance), Amina Yusuf (People), Nandini Wijaya (Legal).
- Exec: Hana Okafor.

## Promotion
Promotions happen in the review cycle only. The manager writes the case, a calibration panel reviews it, and Amina Yusuf records the outcome.

title: DPA guide
author: Nandini Wijaya
text:
# DPA guide
Owner: Nandini Wijaya. Security contact: Jiwon Park. Last reviewed: 17 September 2026.

## What our standard DPA commits to
- We are the processor; the customer is the controller.
- Subprocessors: listed on the trust page. We give customers 30 days notice before adding a new subprocessor.
- Deletion: shipment payloads are deleted within 30 days of a verified tenant deletion request.
- Audit records: retained for 730 days for all tenants, including closed accounts.
- Logs: event IDs and error codes only, never carrier payload bodies.
- Breach notice: Legal and Security notify affected customers without undue delay; support incident notices follow the support SLA.

## Common customer asks
- Shorter subprocessor notice: no. Offer an email subscription to the trust page instead.
- Shorter audit retention: no. Retention is the same for all tenants.
- Residency: only by the Japan residency schedule, after Legal and Security approve. Ask Nandini Wijaya.

title: Security incident response
author: Jiwon Park
text:
# Security incident response
Owner: Jiwon Park. Incident command: Platform on-call primary, escalation to Mei Tan. Last reviewed: 24 September 2026.

## Severity
- SEV1: confirmed exposure of customer data, or attacker access to production.
- SEV2: suspected exposure, or compromise of an employee account with production access.
- SEV3: policy breach with no exposure (for example a payload body found in logs).

## Steps
1. Anyone who suspects an incident posts in #security and pages the on-call primary.
2. The incident commander opens the incident channel and names a scribe.
3. Jiwon Park leads containment: revoke sessions, rotate credentials through the secret store, block vendor access.
4. Siti Nuraini sends the first customer notice within 30 minutes of a confirmed severity-one incident.
5. Nandini Wijaya decides on regulator and contractual notices.
6. Replays of more than 10000 events during recovery need the incident commander's approval.
7. Post-incident review within five business days. Jiwon Park owns the actions list.

## Never
Never paste credentials, tokens or customer payloads into chat or tickets.

title: Vendor access roster review October 2026
author: Jiwon Park

title: Data warehouse guide
author: Linh Nguyen
text:
# Data warehouse guide
Owner: Linh Nguyen (Data). Last reviewed: 22 September 2026.
Tomoko Ito built the first models and left in December 2025; Linh Nguyen owns everything she owned.

## Layout
- raw (BigQuery dataset northwind_raw): loaded from the PostgreSQL replicas and the Kafka event log by the analytics loader. No payload bodies, only IDs, timestamps and status fields.
- staging (northwind_staging): cleaned, one model per source table.
- marts (northwind_marts): shipments, workspaces, billing, support, route_lens_accuracy.

## Loads
- Shipments and tracking events: hourly.
- Billing: nightly, plus a month-start run for invoicing.
- Support tickets: nightly.

## Rules
- Internal demo tenants are excluded from activation metrics through the is_demo_tenant flag.
- Sakura data in the warehouse is aggregated only. Payload-level Sakura data stays in Japan.
- Retention follows the source system. Audit-derived tables keep 730 days.

## Who to ask
Linh Nguyen for models and access. Nur Aziz for billing marts.

title: Metric definitions
author: Linh Nguyen
text:
# Metric definitions
Owner: Linh Nguyen. Effective 15 September 2026.

- Active workspace: a workspace that completes at least one shipment during the calendar week. A login alone does not count.
- Weekly activation rate: active workspaces divided by paid workspaces, excluding internal demo tenants from the denominator.
- Weekly snapshot: frozen at Monday 09:00 Singapore time. Later backfills change the next snapshot, never a frozen one.
- Completed shipment: a shipment with a delivered or proof-of-delivery event. This is also the billing unit.
- Route Lens arrival error: absolute difference between predicted midpoint and actual arrival, reported as a weekly median.
- Pilot shipments: completed shipments in tenants with an active pilot order. This is the primary Q4 company outcome.
- Fleet dashboard freshness: the fleet dashboard is cached for five minutes while ingestion stays below 2000 events per second.

title: Service catalog: kestrel-connector
author: Chen Wei
text:
# Service catalog: kestrel-connector
Owner team: Integrations. Owner: Chen Wei. Last reviewed: 6 October 2026.
Who to ask: Chen Wei for the partner contract and parsing, Haruto Sato for runtime.

## Summary
Polls the Kestrel partner API for each tenant, normalizes envelopes and appends carrier events to Kafka.

## Facts
- Language and framework: Python 3.12, FastAPI for the admin endpoints, an asyncio poller.
- Repo: northwind-platform/connectors/kestrel.
- On-call rota: Integrations weekday primary (Chen Wei), Platform rota covers nights and weekends.
- Datastores: PostgreSQL table connector_cursors in dispatch-db (Singapore) and dispatch-db-jp (Japan, Sakura tenants only).
- Produces: carrier.events.v1 (Kafka, partitioned by tenant and shipment). Poison envelopes go to carrier.events.dlq.
- Consumes: tenant.lifecycle.v1 (stops polling for deleted tenants).
- Upstream: Kestrel partner API over REST (HTTPS polling).
- Downstream: dispatch reads its events from Kafka. No direct calls.

## Limits
- At most two concurrent polling requests per tenant (Kestrel v3 agreement). Larger pages compensate.
- Cursors persist the last accepted ingestion sequence, not carrier occurrence time.

## SLOs
- 99.5 percent of polls complete within 10 seconds, monthly.
- Event lag from partner to Kafka under 2 minutes at p95.

## Dashboards
Grafana Cloud: Kestrel polling (requests by tenant, response class), Connector lag.

## Deploy
GitHub Actions builds an immutable image tagged with the commit SHA; Argo CD promotes the reviewed manifest from northwind-infra. Release slots are Tuesday and Thursday mornings. No production deploys on Fridays, including scheduled jobs and configuration-only releases. Every production change needs a primary and a secondary responder online for the next two hours.

## Runbook
Check the tenant, saved cursor and credential validity in the restricted operations tool before any replay. Record event IDs and the reason. A replay of more than 10000 events needs approval from the incident commander.

title: Service catalog: webhook-gateway
author: Chen Wei
text:
# Service catalog: webhook-gateway
Owner team: Integrations. Owner: Chen Wei. Last reviewed: 6 October 2026.
Who to ask: Chen Wei. Runtime: Haruto Sato.

## Summary
Receives carrier webhooks, checks the partner signature, acknowledges quickly and writes the normalized event to Kafka.

## Facts
- Language and framework: Python 3.12, FastAPI.
- Repo: northwind-platform/connectors/webhooks.
- On-call rota: Integrations weekday primary, Platform rota out of hours.
- Datastores: none of its own. Retry state lives in the Kafka retry topic.
- Produces: carrier.events.v1, carrier.webhooks.retry, carrier.events.dlq.
- Consumes: carrier.webhooks.retry.
- Upstream: carrier platforms call POST /hooks/carrier/{partner} over REST (HTTPS).
- Downstream: dispatch through Kafka.

## Retry rule
Retry a failed carrier webhook for at most six hours, then move it to the dead-letter topic. The dead-letter handling is unchanged from the 24 hour era.

## SLOs
- 99.9 percent of webhook requests acknowledged within 500 milliseconds.
- Dead-letter topic reviewed every business day by Chen Wei.

## Dashboards
Grafana Cloud: Webhook intake, Retry and DLQ depth.

## Deploy
GitHub Actions builds an immutable image tagged with the commit SHA; Argo CD promotes the reviewed manifest from northwind-infra. Release slots are Tuesday and Thursday mornings. No production deploys on Fridays, including scheduled jobs and configuration-only releases. Every production change needs a primary and a secondary responder online for the next two hours.

## Runbook
On a DLQ spike, check signature failures first, then partner status. Log event IDs and error codes only, never payload bodies.

title: Service catalog: dispatch
author: Mei Tan
text:
# Service catalog: dispatch
Owner team: Platform. Owner: Mei Tan. Main contributors: Pranav Menon, Haruto Sato. Last reviewed: 7 October 2026.
Anika Rao designed the first version and left on 30 June 2026. Mei Tan owns her platform decisions.

## Summary
Consumes carrier and scanner events, deduplicates them, applies them to shipment state in PostgreSQL and publishes acknowledgements and state changes.

## Facts
- Language and framework: Python 3.12, FastAPI for internal endpoints, Kafka consumer workers.
- Repo: northwind-platform/services/dispatch.
- On-call rota: Platform (primary Haruto Sato or Pranav Menon by week, secondary Mei Tan).
- Datastores: PostgreSQL 16 on Cloud SQL, dispatch-db (Singapore) and dispatch-db-jp (Japan). Tables: shipments, shipment_events, dedup_keys, dispatch_flush_settings.
- Produces: shipment.state.v1, dispatch.acks.v1 (feeds the ACK age dashboards).
- Consumes: carrier.events.v1, scanner.manifests.v1, booking.events.v1, tenant.lifecycle.v1.
- Upstream: kestrel-connector, webhook-gateway, scanner-sync and booking-api through Kafka.
- Downstream: ledger, eta, notify and analytics-loader through Kafka; tracking-api reads the replica.

## Rules carried in code
- Deduplication key is tenant_id plus carrier_event_id, retained for seven days.
- Event occurrence time is stored apart from ingestion sequence.
- Flush settings are read from the dispatch_flush_settings table between batches (since September 2026). A row change is a configuration-only production release.

## SLOs
- Oldest unacknowledged event (ACK age) under 60 seconds for 99 percent of minutes.
- Consumer lag under 5000 events at p95.

## Dashboards
Grafana Cloud: Dispatch ACK age, Consumer lag by tenant, Release annotations.

## Deploy
GitHub Actions builds an immutable image tagged with the commit SHA; Argo CD promotes the reviewed manifest from northwind-infra. Release slots are Tuesday and Thursday mornings. No production deploys on Fridays, including scheduled jobs and configuration-only releases. Every production change needs a primary and a secondary responder online for the next two hours.

## Runbook
Watch ACK age, not pod health. Compare with the last release SHA. Roll back with the reference on the release ticket.

text:
# Service catalog: eta
Owner team: Platform, with Data for model evaluation. Owner: Mei Tan. Model evaluation: Linh Nguyen. Last reviewed: 8 October 2026.

## Summary
Returns the Route Lens arrival range for a shipment. Calls the route-model inference endpoint and falls back to the last carrier ETA when the model is slow.

## Facts
- Language and framework: Python 3.12, gRPC server (grpcio).
- Repo: northwind-platform/services/eta.
- On-call rota: Platform.
- Datastores: Redis cache-tracking for short-lived results; reads shipment state from the dispatch-db replica.
- Produces: eta.predictions.v1 (for accuracy analysis).
- Consumes: shipment.state.v1.
- Upstream: tracking-api over gRPC.
- Downstream: route-model inference over gRPC. The serving configuration is owned in a separate decision record.

## Rules carried in code
- After 600 milliseconds without a route-model response, return the last carrier ETA with its observed_at timestamp.
- Always return an estimated range, never a guaranteed delivery time.

## SLOs
- p95 under 700 milliseconds end to end, including fallback.
- Weekly median absolute arrival error is tracked on the Route Lens accuracy gate dashboard.

## Dashboards
Grafana Cloud: ETA latency and fallback rate. Warehouse: Route Lens accuracy gate (Aisha Rahman, Linh Nguyen).

## Deploy
GitHub Actions builds an immutable image tagged with the commit SHA; Argo CD promotes the reviewed manifest from northwind-infra. Release slots are Tuesday and Thursday mornings. External carriers and partners

  Carrier platforms    -- REST webhook -->  webhook-gateway

kestrel-connector
  event carrier.events.v1 --> dispatch, analytics-loader

webhook-gateway
  event carrier.events.v1 --> dispatch, analytics-loader

  writes PostgreSQL dispatch-db, dispatch-db-jp

title: Database and data store access
author: Mei Tan
text:
# Database and data store access
Owner: Mei Tan. Security reviewer: Jiwon Park. Last reviewed: 12 October 2026.
Raise every request in the access request form with the store, purpose and end date. Access goes to a group, never to a person, and ends on the end date.

## PostgreSQL dispatch-db (Cloud SQL, Singapore)
- Owner: Mei Tan. Schemas: shipments, bookings, ledger, audit, tenants, connector_cursors.
- Read (replica): approver Mei Tan. Ledger view for Finance: approver Nur Aziz with Mei Tan.
- Write: no standing human write. Break-glass write needs Mei Tan and Jiwon Park and an incident ticket.
- Retention: shipment payloads deleted within 30 days of a verified tenant deletion request; audit records 730 days.

## PostgreSQL dispatch-db-jp (Cloud SQL, Japan, Sakura)
- Owner: Mei Tan. Same schemas as dispatch-db.
- Read: approver Mei Tan and Jiwon Park. Write: break-glass only, as above.
- Sakura payloads and their backups stay in Japan. No exports out of region.

## Kafka (managed cluster)
- Owner: Haruto Sato for operation, Mei Tan for topic design. Connector topics: Chen Wei.
- Produce or consume ACLs: approver Mei Tan. Connector topics also need Chen Wei.
- Retention: 7 days on event topics, 14 days on carrier.events.dlq.

## Redis cache-tracking
- Owner: Haruto Sato. Disposable acceleration only. No human access; services only.
- The Redis idem-store was retired in June 2026. Booking idempotency tokens now live in the PostgreSQL bookings schema (table booking_idempotency), kept for seven days and scoped to the tenant.

## BigQuery (northwind_raw, northwind_staging, northwind_marts)
- Owner: Linh Nguyen. Marts read: Linh Nguyen. Raw and staging read: Linh Nguyen and Jiwon Park. Write: Data team service accounts only.
- Retention: follows the source; audit-derived tables 730 days.

## Cloud Storage (pod-photos-sg, pod-photos-jp, backups-sg, backups-jp)
- Owner: Pranav Menon for photos, Mei Tan for backups. Read: Jiwon Park approves. Write: services only.
- Restore drills run every quarter from backups using an isolated tenant fixture. Sakura drills use backups-jp only.

## Unleash (feature flags)
- Owner: Mei Tan. Changes to production flags are configuration releases and follow the release slots.
